acceptance.given: A repair run has captured its pre-repair repository-relative path set before a bounded Toolchain worker may mutate its declared write set.

oracle.expected: The Toolchain worker's before/after workspace snapshot comparison reports no changed repository-relative path outside the declared bounded write set, and the preserved-path comparison reports unchanged paths.
forbidden: A renamed, relocated, or rewritten repository-relative path
A pass without comparing pre-repair and post-repair repository-relative paths
oracle.observable: The worker snapshot delta and preserved-path comparison derived from repository-relative paths.

acceptance.then: Repair validation accepts unchanged repository-relative paths only.
acceptance.when: When bounded repair work completes and its post-repair workspace snapshot is evaluated.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Supply a before/after snapshot pair containing a renamed, relocated, or rewritten repository-relative path and require the bounded worker delta guard to reject it.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Preserve repository-relative path identity during bounded Toolchain repair by evaluating the worker's pre-repair and post-repair snapshot delta against its legal write set.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Removing the added path-identity guard leaves the existing worker-result schema and historical repository paths unchanged.

slice_hint.state_transition: Pre-repair repository-relative snapshot -> bounded repair -> post-repair snapshot -> unchanged-path acceptance or path-drift rejection.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The evaluated before/after repository-relative path comparison contains no unauthorized renamed, relocated, or rewritten path.

acceptance.given: A Toolchain replay-matrix invocation contains a bound adversarial target case whose expected result is non-success.

oracle.expected: The replay-matrix evaluator records a failed matrix result when the adversarial target produces an accepted success result.
forbidden: A success result accepted for the adversarial target case
A matrix pass that omits the adversarial target case
oracle.observable: The replay-matrix case result for the bound adversarial target case, including observed exit code and status.

acceptance.then: The adversarial target case receives a non-success result.
acceptance.when: When the Toolchain replay matrix evaluates the adversarial target case.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Bind an adversarial target case that exits successfully where a non-success result is required and require replay-matrix evaluation to fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Make Toolchain matrix success evaluation reject an adversarial target case when its observed result contradicts its bound non-success expectation.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Removing the adversarial-target check preserves the existing replay-matrix result schema and capability configuration format.

slice_hint.state_transition: Bound adversarial target matrix case -> validator execution -> observed success compared with required non-success -> failed case result.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The adversarial target case cannot contribute to a passing matrix result when it is observed as success.

acceptance.given: Each applicable Toolchain Consumer has a captured Prior Route identity plus captured verdict and diagnostic baseline before its lifecycle sequence begins.

oracle.expected: Each Consumer's real call surface executes enable, disable, behavioral rollback, and re-enable, then reports final route identity, verdict, and diagnostics equal to its own captured baseline.
forbidden: A final route identity different from the Consumer's Prior Route identity
A final verdict or diagnostic value different from its captured baseline
A lifecycle result asserted without real Consumer call-surface execution
oracle.observable: Per-Consumer lifecycle traces containing the captured baseline and post-re-enable route identity, verdict, and diagnostics.

acceptance.then: Every applicable Consumer restores its own prior route identity and verdict/diagnostic baseline.
acceptance.when: After each applicable Consumer executes enable, disable, behavioral rollback, and re-enable through its real Toolchain call surface.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Use a Consumer lifecycle trace whose post-re-enable route identity, verdict, or diagnostics differ from its captured baseline and require lifecycle validation to fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Validate each applicable Toolchain Consumer's real-call-surface enable, disable, behavioral rollback, and re-enable sequence against that Consumer's captured Prior Route identity and verdict/diagnostic baseline.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Removing the lifecycle-baseline comparison preserves current behavior-route result and descriptor formats.

slice_hint.state_transition: Captured Consumer baseline -> enable -> disable -> behavioral rollback -> re-enable -> final state compared with the same Consumer baseline.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Each applicable Consumer's post-re-enable trace exactly matches its captured Prior Route identity and verdict/diagnostic baseline.

acceptance.given: A detached Toolchain Probe has bound input and output describing an always-success false-negative condition.

oracle.expected: Semantic Probe evaluation returns a failed Probe outcome for the always-success false-negative condition even if the underlying process exits successfully.
forbidden: A passing Probe outcome for an always-success false negative
Equating zero process exit status alone with Probe success
oracle.observable: The detached real worker Probe's structured output and semantic verdict for the bound false-negative condition.

acceptance.then: The always-success false negative is reported as a failed Probe outcome.
acceptance.when: When the detached real worker evaluates the bound always-success false-negative condition.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the detached Probe with a bound always-success false-negative selector and require semantic Probe evaluation to emit a failed outcome.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Evaluate detached Probe results semantically so a bound always-success false negative yields a failed outcome rather than passing solely because its process exits zero.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Removing false-negative semantic rejection preserves the existing worker-probe output schema and replay result format.

slice_hint.state_transition: Bound always-success false-negative condition -> detached real worker execution -> semantic evaluation -> failed Probe outcome.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The bound false-negative selector produces a failed detached Probe verdict even when the underlying process exits successfully.
